title: Split an affine etale morphism near a marked geometric fibre
statement:
Let $S$ and $U$ be affine schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum], let $f:U\to S$ be etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], and let $\bar s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$ be a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point] with image $s$. There are an affine pointed etale neighbourhood $(V,\bar v)$ of $\bar s$ [def-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhoods], a nonnegative integer $n$, and a decomposition over $V$
$$U\times_S V\ \cong\ \left(\coprod_{i=1}^n V\right)\amalg W,$$
where $W\to V$ is etale. The fibre of $V\to S$ over $s$ has exactly one underlying point, the image of $\bar v$, and $W$ has no point mapping to $s$ under $W\to V\to S$. Here the fibre product is [def-pc-fibre-product], and the coproduct is the disjoint union of schemes with its evident structure morphism. In particular the $n$ copy inclusions, composed with the projection to $U$ and with $\bar v$, give a bijection $\{1,\ldots,n\}\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_S(\operatorname{Spec}\Omega,U)$.

source.place: Tag 04HM, lemma-etale-etale-local-technical, applied to all points of the finite fibre; the affine and single-s-fibre-point refinement is the third paragraph of etale-cohomology.tex Tag 04HU, lemma-points-small-etale-site, after restricting S to an affine open. Fibre structure: morphisms.tex Tag 02GL, lemma-etale-over-field (2).

proof.text: The morphism $f$ is separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-source-morphism-separated], since its source $U$ is affine. By [def-weil-etale-morphism], $f$ is unramified, as well as flat and locally of finite presentation. Thus it is unramified at every point of the fibre over $s$.

source.place: Tag 04HU, lemma-points-small-etale-site, proof, third paragraph: affine U is separated

proof.text: Write $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ and $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ using affine coordinates. The fibre $U_s=U\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], and hence quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. It is discrete by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-fibre-discrete-separable-points]. Its open covering by singleton subsets therefore has a finite subcover. Via the fibre homeomorphism in [def-pc-scheme-fibre], enumerate the underlying points of $f^{-1}(s)$ without repetitions as $x_1,\ldots,x_r$, allowing $r=0$.

source.place: Tag 04HU, lemma-points-small-etale-site, proof, third paragraph; morphisms.tex Tag 02GL, lemma-etale-over-field (2); schemes.tex Tag 01I4, lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes

proof.text:
Apply [lem-weil-pbc-unramified-etale-local-decomposition] to $f$ and all $x_1,\ldots,x_r$. Its hypotheses hold by steps 1 and 2. Obtain an etale $g_0:T_0\to S$, a point $t\in T_0$ above $s$, and a finite clopen decomposition
$$U\times_S T_0=W_0\amalg\coprod_a P_a.$$
Each $h_a:P_a\to T_0$ is a closed immersion whose image contains $t$. The final clause of the cited statement gives $(W_0)_t=\varnothing$, since the list contains every point over $s$.

source.place: Tag 04HI, lemma-unramified-etale-local-technical, applied as in the proof of Tag 04HM, lemma-etale-etale-local-technical

proof.text: The projection $U\times_S T_0\to T_0$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change]. Each inclusion $P_a\hookrightarrow U\times_S T_0$ and the inclusion of $W_0$ are open immersions. They are etale, and composing with the projection shows that every $h_a$ and $W_0\to T_0$ are etale, by clauses (1) and (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation].

source.place: Tag 04HM, lemma-etale-etale-local-technical, proof: the closed-immersion pieces are etale; morphisms.tex Tags 02GO, 02GP, 02GN

proof.text: Each $h_a$ is a monomorphism. Indeed a closed immersion is injective on underlying spaces and has a locally surjective structure-sheaf map by [def-weil-closed-immersion]. If $b,c:Z\to P_a$ satisfy $h_ab=h_ac$, injectivity gives the same continuous map. Locally lift sections of $\mathcal O_{P_a}$ through $\mathcal O_{T_0}\to(h_a)_*\mathcal O_{P_a}$; equality after composition gives equality on those lifts, hence on all sections and on their germs. Thus $b=c$ as scheme morphisms.

source.place: Tag 04HM, lemma-etale-etale-local-technical, proof, application of Tag 025G; monomorphism verification directly from the definition of a closed immersion

proof.text: Since $h_a$ is etale, it is flat and locally of finite presentation by [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Together with step 5 these are exactly the hypotheses of [lem-pe-flat-lfp-monomorphism-open]. Hence each $h_a$ is an open immersion. By [def-weil-open-immersion] it identifies $P_a$ with the open subscheme on $O_a=h_a(P_a)\subseteq T_0$, and $t\in O_a$ by step 3.

source.place: Tag 025G, theorem-etale-radicial-open, implication (3) to (1), as used in Tag 04HM

proof.text:
There are only finitely many $a$, so $O=\bigcap_a O_a$ is open and contains $t$; if there are no pieces put $O=T_0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis], choose an affine open $T$ with $t\in T\subseteq O$. Restrict the decomposition to $T$. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product] these are the actual inverse-image open subschemes, with their inherited structure sheaves. Each $P_a\times_{T_0}T$ is isomorphic to $T$, since $P_a$ is the open subscheme $O_a$ and $T\subseteq O_a$. Thus
$$U\times_S T\cong W_T\amalg\coprod_{a=1}^n T,$$
where $n$ is the number of pieces, and $(W_T)_t$ is empty. The map $g:T\to S$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation].

source.place: Tag 04HM, lemma-etale-etale-local-technical, proof, replacing the base by the intersection of the images; affine refinement by schemes.tex Tag 01IT, lemma-basis-affine-opens

proof.text: The fibre $T_s=T\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], and discrete by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-fibre-discrete-separable-points], applied to the etale map $g$. The singleton open covering again has a finite subcover. By [def-pc-scheme-fibre], the subspace $g^{-1}(s)\subseteq T$ is a finite discrete space. Write its points as $t,y_1,\ldots,y_m$.

source.place: Tag 04HU, lemma-points-small-etale-site, third proof paragraph: shrinking V to have exactly one point over s; finiteness by morphisms.tex Tag 02GL and schemes.tex Tag 01I4

proof.text:
For each $j$, the point $t$ is not in $\overline{\{y_j\}}\subseteq T$: otherwise it would belong to the closure of $\{y_j\}$ in the subspace $g^{-1}(s)$, contrary to discreteness. Consequently
$$H=T\setminus\bigcup_{j=1}^m\overline{\{y_j\}}$$
is an open neighbourhood of $t$ containing none of the $y_j$. Choose an affine open $V$ with $t\in V\subseteq H$ by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. The fibre of $V\to S$ over $s$ has exactly one point, namely $t$ viewed as a point of $V$; denote it by $v$. The restricted map $V\to S$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation].

source.place: Tag 04HU, lemma-points-small-etale-site, third proof paragraph: details of the shrinking to one point; schemes.tex Tag 01IT

proof.text:
Restrict the decomposition of step 7 from $T$ to $V$. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product] and the universal property [def-pc-fibre-product], restriction preserves the disjoint open cover and each copy of $T$ restricts to a copy of $V$. Put $W=W_T\times_TV$. Then
$$U\times_S V\cong\left(\coprod_{a=1}^n V\right)\amalg W.$$
The map $W\to V$ is etale: it is the composite of its open inclusion into $U\times_SV$ with the etale projection, using [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. Its fibre over $v$ is empty by step 7. If $w\in W$ mapped to $s$, its image in $V$ would have to be $v$ by step 9, a contradiction. Thus $W$ has no point mapping to $s$.

source.place: Tag 04HU, lemma-points-small-etale-site, third proof paragraph, conclusion that W has no point over s; etale.tex Tag 04HM

proof.text: Choose a lift $\bar v:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to V$ of $\bar s$ with image $v$ using the final sentence of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-cover-geometric-point-lift]. To put this application literally under its covering hypothesis, use the jointly surjective etale family $\{V\to S,\operatorname{id}_S\}$; the identity is an open immersion and hence etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. The cited final sentence permits the prescribed member $V$ and its prescribed point $v$. The field remains $\Omega$. Hence $(V,\bar v)$ is a pointed etale neighbourhood by [def-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhoods], and it is affine by construction.

source.place: Tag 03PR, lemma-geometric-lift-to-cover; Tag 04HU, lemma-points-small-etale-site, choice of pointed neighbourhood

proof.text: By [def-pc-fibre-product], sending $a:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to U$ over $S$ to $(a,\bar v)$ is a bijection from $\operatorname{Hom}_S(\operatorname{Spec}\Omega,U)$ to $\operatorname{Hom}_V(\operatorname{Spec}\Omega,U\times_SV)$, where the map to $V$ on the source is fixed to be $\bar v$. The spectrum of a field has one point by [def-weil-affine-spectrum], so every such morphism factors through exactly one member of the disjoint open decomposition of step 10, using the restricted-sheaf description [def-weil-open-immersion]. It cannot factor through $W$, since its point would then map to $s$. For each copy of $V$ there is exactly one morphism over $V$, namely $\bar v$ followed by that copy inclusion. Taking the first projection gives exactly the $n$ lifts specified in the statement, and proves the bijection, also when $n=0$.

source.place: Tag 04HU, lemma-points-small-etale-site, third proof paragraph, geometric fibre count; explicit fibre-product argument for the stated bijection

lean.statement: theorem exists_affine_etale_split_neighbourhood {S U : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine S] [IsAffine U] (f : U ⟶ S) [Etale f] (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (bar_s : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ S) (s : S) (hs : bar_s (IsLocalRing.closedPoint Ω) = s) : ∃ (V : Scheme.{u}) (g : V ⟶ S) (_ : IsAffine V) (_ : Etale g), ∃ (bar_v : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ V), bar_v ≫ g = bar_s ∧ ∃ (n : ℕ) (W : Scheme.{u}) (w : W ⟶ V) (_ : Etale w), ∃ (e : pullback f g ≅ (∐ fun _ : Fin n => V) ⨿ W), e.hom ≫ coprod.desc (Sigma.desc (fun _ : Fin n => 𝟙 V)) w = pullback.snd f g ∧ (∀ x : V, g x = s ↔ x = bar_v (IsLocalRing.closedPoint Ω)) ∧ (∀ x : W, (w ≫ g) x ≠ s) ∧ ∃ (a : Fin n → (Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ U)), (∀ i : Fin n, a i = bar_v ≫ Sigma.ι (fun _ : Fin n => V) i ≫ coprod.inl ≫ e.inv ≫ pullback.fst f g) ∧ ∃ (ha : ∀ i : Fin n, a i ≫ f = bar_s), ∃ (E : Fin n ≃ {q : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ U // q ≫ f = bar_s}), ∀ i : Fin n, E i = ⟨a i, ha i⟩
